<thought>The mass spectrum shows a clear M+1 peak at ~9% of the monoisotopic intensity and much smaller higher‑order peaks, which matches the characteristic isotopic pattern of carbon (13C ≈1.1% per carbon). No significant M+2 peak (~33% for Cl or ~100% for Br) is observed, so chlorine, bromine, sulfur, etc., cannot be definitively identified. Therefore, carbon is the only element that can be definitively identified from the observed isotopic distribution.</thought>
<final_answer>['C']</final_answer>
